sections.label: Workplace fatality rate target
sections.summary: Tripartite partners targeted reducing workplace fatality rate from 3.1 per 100,000 workers in 2006 to below 1.8 by 2018, reaching 1.9 in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Together with our tripartite partners, we set a target to reduce our workplace fatality rate from 3.1 per 100,000 workers in 2006 to less than 1.8 per 100,000 workers by 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Through the collective efforts of the industry and tripartite partners, the workplace fatality rate fell to 1.9 in 2016.

sections.label: SMRT fined for employee deaths
sections.summary: SMRT was fined $400,000 for systemic failures resulting in the deaths of two employees this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: For example, the Singapore Mass Rapid Transit (SMRT) was fined $400,000 for systemic failures resulting in the deaths of two employees this year.

sections.label: Clause 7(c) raises SL penalty
sections.summary: Clause 7(c) of the Bill raises the maximum penalty under the SL by 2.5 times, from $20,000 to $50,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Clause 7(c) of the Bill will, therefore, raise the maximum penalty under the SL by 2.5 times, from $20,000 to $50,000.

sections.label: Clause 3 allows learning reports
sections.summary: Clause 3 of the Bill allows the Commissioner for WSH to release a learning report before legal proceedings have concluded.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Clause 3 of the Bill will, therefore, allow the Commissioner for WSH to release a learning report before legal proceedings have concluded.

sections.label: Learning reports inadmissible in proceedings
sections.summary: Learning reports will be inadmissible in any civil, criminal, disciplinary, arbitral or work injury compensation proceedings to safeguard parties' interests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: To safeguard the interests of the parties involved, learning reports will be inadmissible in any civil, criminal, disciplinary, arbitral or work injury compensation proceedings.

sections.label: Workers trained in safety courses
sections.summary: Annually, over 150,000 workers are trained in basic safety orientation courses offered by about 80 ATP-accredited training providers under MOM.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Annually, over 150,000 workers are trained in basic safety orientation courses offered by about 80 training providers accredited under the Approved Training Provider (ATP) scheme by MOM.

sections.label: WSQ courses migration progress
sections.summary: 23 WSQ courses have been developed and offered by SSG-accredited providers, with migration of the remaining 33 expected by 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: So far, 23 courses have been developed under the WSQ system and offered by SSG-accredited training providers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: We expect the migration of the remaining 33 courses to be completed by 2019.

sections.label: Clause 6 liability protection
sections.summary: Clause 6 extends personal liability protection to the Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, inspectors and authorised officers for acts done in good faith and with reasonable care under the WSH Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Clause 6 will extend the scope of personal liability protection to the Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, inspectors and authorised officers for acts done in good faith and with reasonable care in carrying out their duties under the WSH Act properly and professionally.

sections.label: Government liability and fatality target
sections.summary: The Government and its officers remain liable for negligent acts or acts beyond legal powers, and the changes support a target of under one fatality per 100,000 workers before 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The Government and its officers remain liable for negligent acts or for acts beyond their legal powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: These changes will further strengthen the foundation for a stronger prevention mindset and are important steps as we move towards our next target of reducing the workplace fatality rate to less than one per 100,000 workers before 2028.

sections.label: WSH 2028 strategy engagement
sections.summary: Over the next few months, tripartite partners and industry stakeholders will be engaged to co-develop the WSH 2028 national strategy for the next decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Over the next few months, we will engage our tripartite partners and industry stakeholders to co-develop the WSH 2028 national strategy for the next decade.

sections.label: Workplace fatality rate progress
sections.summary: Workplace fatalities fell from 4.9 per 100,000 workers in 2004 to 1.9 in 2016, with targets of 1.8 by 2018 and below one by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In over a decade, we have made progress based on these key principles in reducing our workplace fatalities from 4.9 per 100,000 workers in 2004, to 2.8 per 100,000 workers in 2008, and further to 1.9 per 100,000 workers in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In the first half of 2017, there have been 19 fatal work accidents, compared to 66 workplace accident fatalities in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: By 2018, we are striving to reach our WSH2018 target of 1.8 fatalities per 100,000 workers, and our next target is to go below one fatality per 100,000 workers by 2028.

sections.label: Increased maximum fine under SL
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to reinforce prevention culture by increasing the maximum fine that can be prescribed under SL from $20,000 to $50,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: One of the ways through which the Bill seeks to reinforce the prevention culture is by increasing the maximum fine that can be prescribed under SL from $20,000 to $50,000.

sections.label: WSH training curriculum review
sections.summary: Asks whether SSG will work with MOM subject matter experts to review WSH training curriculum, and proposes engaging industry associations, practitioners, unions and workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, I would like to ask the Minister whether SSG will continue to work with subject matter experts from MOM to review the curriculum of WSH training to ensure their relevance, or if the subject matter experts will be persons within SSG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I would also like to propose that in forming the curriculum of the training, industry associations, practitioners, unions and our working people should be engaged in the process to ensure that the training delivered is relevant, practical, tailored to the needs of each industry and endorsed by the industry.

sections.label: Increasing fines for deterrence
sections.summary: The first measure is to strengthen deterrence by increasing fines to prevent accidents from recurring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The first is to strengthen deterrence by increasing the fines to prevent the recurrence of accidents.

sections.label: Professional training transferred to SSG
sections.summary: Professional training was previously under MOM's purview and has now been transferred to SSG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Third, professional training used to be under the purview of MOM and is now transferred to SSG.

sections.label: Tripartite effort for safety culture
sections.summary: Tripartite partners and industry stakeholders, including training providers, must collectively go beyond compliance to build a safety culture benefiting all stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The tripartite partners and industry stakeholders, including training providers, have to take concerted effort collectively to go beyond compliance to build a culture of safety which will result in a true win-win-win for all stakeholders so that every workplace is a safer workplace, every worker a safer worker and every employer, a safer employer.

sections.label: Fatal injury rate decline
sections.summary: The fatal injury rate fell from 4.9 per 100,000 employed persons in 2004 to the targeted 1.8 in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The rate of fatal injuries came down from 4.9 per 100,000 employed persons in 2004 to the targeted 1.8 in 2014.

sections.label: Fatal injury rate rebound
sections.summary: The fatal injury rate rose again and hovered at 1.9 in the last two years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The rate of fatal injuries bounced back up and hovered at 1.9 in the last two years.

sections.label: Learning report evidence admissibility
sections.summary: The new section 27B(3) allows the learning report to be admissible as evidence in three types of inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This will protect the objectives of the learning report.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, the new section 27B(3) allows for the learning report to be admissible as evidence in three types of inquiry.

sections.label: Workplace health fatality percentage
sections.summary: The percentage of fatalities with workplace health as a contributory factor rose to one-third in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The percentage of fatalities with workplace health as a contributory factor rose to one-third in 2014.

sections.label: Under-reporting study proposed
sections.summary: Occupational Skin Disease cases doubled in the first half of 2017, and a study on under-reporting of accidents and occupational diseases is proposed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, the number of cases of Occupational Skin Disease doubled in the first half of 2017, which MOM said was likely due to greater awareness of reporting requirements.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I believe it is timely for the Government to commission a study on the scale and causes of under-reporting of accidents and occupational diseases.

sections.label: Doctors reporting workplace accidents
sections.summary: It asks why doctors are not required to report suspected workplace accidents, especially for hospitalisation of at least 24 hours or medical certificates over three days.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Now, surely, this applies to workplace safety and the reporting of accidents, too.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, why not require doctors to report any suspected workplace accidents, especially when a worker is hospitalised for at least 24 hours or given a medical certificate for more than three days?

sections.label: Required reporting by doctors
sections.summary: Required reporting is part of the learning culture of the WSH 2018 Plus framework, and the Government is urged to consider required reporting by doctors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Required reporting is part of the learning culture that the WSH 2018 Plus framework is trying to promote.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to consider required reporting by doctors of injuries suspected to be caused by workplace accidents.

sections.label: Public incident learning report
sections.summary: The Bill allows the Commissioner for WSH to make public a detailed incident learning report before any prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill sets out to allow the Commissioner for WSH to make public a detailed incident learning report before any prosecution.

sections.label: WSH penalties deterrence
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes stricter WSH penalties but says the maximum penalty amount seems not much of a deterrent, especially with loss of life.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Enhancing deterrence through more stringent WSH penalties is welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, the maximum penalty amount does not seem to be much of a deterrent, especially when there is loss of life or lives.

sections.label: Workplace abuse and harassment inclusion
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether workplace abuse and harassment can be more clearly included in WSH requirements and employer obligations to provide a safe work environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To present greater weightage to this issue of abuse and harassment at the workplace, can there be a more defined inclusion of workplace abuse and harassment incorporated into the WSH requirement and obligation by employers so as to provide a safe work environment for the employees?

sections.label: PM Lee workplace fatality target
sections.summary: At the World Congress on Safety and Health At Work, Prime Minister Lee set a target to reduce Singapore's workplace fatality rate to below 1.0 per 100,000 workers by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At the opening of the World Congress on Safety and Health At Work in September this year, Prime Minister Lee set a target for Singapore to reduce our workplace fatality rate to below 1.0 per 100,000 workers by 2028, down from the current 1.9 per 100,000 workers.

sections.label: Return-To-Work programme and accreditation
sections.summary: The speaker notes the WSHC launched the Return-To-Work programme and asks if the Ministry can accredit more in-house coordinators so companies can tap Government funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Since then, NTUC has been working closely with our tripartite partners on this and I am heartened that the Return-To-Work (RTW) programme was launched by WSHC just last week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The programme will see the WSHC working with our public hospitals to provide early intervention for workers who are injured in the course of their work, as well as enable companies to help their workers gradually ease back into their jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Ideally, such in-house coordinators should be the future of the RTW programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, because these coordinators are not accredited, companies are unable to currently tap on any Government funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry work towards accrediting more of such in-house coordinators so as to allow companies to be able to tap on Government funding?

sections.label: Legislating RTW framework
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Ministry would consider legislating the RTW framework to help injured workers recover and reintegrate, and says physical health and mental well-being are lacking in WSH efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider legislating the RTW framework, or at least some aspects of it, at some point in time to better protect our workers and help those who are injured recover and reintegrate back to work quickly, so that their livelihoods are not adversely affected?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Physical health and mental well-being, however, are sorely lacking in our current WSH efforts and conversations.

sections.label: Total WSH
sections.summary: The speaker says that just as there is Total Defence, Singapore must endeavour for Total WSH.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Just as we have Total Defence, we must endeavour for Total WSH.

sections.label: Companies with poor safety records
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry evaluates and removes companies that repeatedly flout safety regulations from the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In line with the movement, it is important to ensure that companies with a chequered past are not given the opportunity to be awarded contracts for key public projects, certainly with heavy scrutinising to ensure that they have put in clear systems to rectify their lapses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: If we truly desire to have zero accidents and fatalities, we must have a more robust system of ensuring that only companies with a clean record or good remedial measures are given such larger jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Does the Ministry have a system of evaluation where companies that have flouted safety regulations repeatedly are taken out of circulation and prevented from being in the industry again?

sections.label: WSH training provider accreditation
sections.summary: States the Bill removes the requirement for the Commissioner to accredit WSH training providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: One of the provisions of this Bill is to have the requirement for the Commissioner to accredit WSH training providers to be removed.

sections.label: Enhanced fines and occupational diseases
sections.summary: Asks whether enhanced fines apply to offences that lead to or increase risk of occupational diseases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify whether the enhanced fines apply to offences that lead to or increase the risk of occupational diseases?

sections.label: Safety equipment and training costs
sections.summary: Asks whether safety equipment and training fall under section 12(1) and cannot be recovered from workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm that the provision of safety equipment and training is part of the measures necessary to ensure the health and safety of employees under section 12(1), and that employers cannot recover such costs from workers?

sections.label: Inspections of workers' actual hours
sections.summary: Asks whether WSH inspectors will check workers' actual hours clocked, since plans may not be complied with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that MOM's inspections on companies’ compliance with the Employment Act found that most have complied with working hour provisions and that WSH inspectors examine plans to manage workers' fatigue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, will WSH inspectors also include as part of their inspections the actual number of hours clocked by workers as plans may not always be complied with in the face of punishing completion deadlines and limited manpower?

sections.label: Safeguards for dismissed worker informants
sections.summary: Asks about notification to MOM when workers are dismissed within two years of assisting authorities, and notes civil society accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Minister consider additional safeguards, such as requiring notification to MOM, where workers are dismissed within two years of providing such assistance to authorities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, in the course of providing direct service to injured migrant workers, civil society organisations often hear first-hand accounts of safety-related issues on worksites that lead to workplace injuries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While MOM's inspections may find that the vast majority of employers are compliant with safety and health requirements, there may be a group of recalcitrant employers with weak safety mindsets that is tarnishing workplace safety culture as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The first-hand accounts that civil society organisations have are valuable because they provide an insight into the practices of this group of employers, which will help MOM in focusing its efforts and resources in addressing the worst violations.

sections.label: Worker accounts and WSH plan
sections.summary: Hearing workers' accounts gauges policy effectiveness, and the speaker welcomes MOM's plan to reach WSH 2018 Plus goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hearing first-hand accounts from the workers is the best way of gauging the effectiveness of our policies and efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am encouraged by the bold plan MOM has articulated to improve WSH and look forward to the steps that can be taken to achieve our objective of becoming a centre of excellence that WSH 2018 Plus envisions.

sections.label: Course conduct and training centres
sections.summary: The passage asks how courses are conducted and audited, and notes training centres in India, Bangladesh and Myanmar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How are the courses conducted and do we do sufficient audits that the workers have adequate understanding of the materials provided to them?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I understand that several training centres are already set up in countries, such as India, Bangladesh and Myanmar, to introduce workers to basic construction techniques.

sections.label: Higher deterrent and fatality target
sections.summary: The supplementary legislation raises the deterrent from $200,000 to $500,000, and Singapore aims for under one fatality per 100,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A higher deterrent, as introduced in the supplementary legislation, raising from $200,000 to $500,000, is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong, at the Official Opening of the World Congress of Safety and Health at Work on 3 September this year, said that Singapore hopes to reduce the number of incidents at the workplace to less than one worker per 100,000 in 10 years' time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Singapore's workplace fatality rate currently stands at 1.9 deaths per 100,000 workers.

sections.label: Learning reports for selected accidents
sections.summary: Learning reports will be issued only for accidents where early sharing can prevent serious accidents in other companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: First, learning reports will not be issued for all workplace accidents, only those where the learning value from early sharing can prevent potential serious accidents in other companies.

sections.label: Delay sharing investigation findings
sections.summary: Investigation ended in October 2014, but findings could only be shared 16 months later after criminal proceedings concluded in February 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Even though we completed our investigation in October 2014, 11 months after the accident, we had to wait a further 16 months before we could share the findings when criminal Court proceedings concluded in February 2016.

sections.label: Learning report inadmissibility
sections.summary: The learning report is inadmissible in civil, criminal, disciplinary, arbitral or work injury compensation proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Second, as I have stated earlier, the learning report is inadmissible in any civil, criminal, disciplinary, arbitral or work injury compensation proceedings.

sections.label: Increased penalty for SL offences
sections.summary: The increased penalty of $50,000 applies to offences under SL, typically when no harm has occurred yet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: The increased penalty of $50,000 is for offences committed under SL, typically when no harm has occurred yet.

sections.label: Non-price weightage in tenders
sections.summary: From January 2018, non-price weightage in the Price-Quality Tender Evaluation Method will rise to between 40% and 60% for building projects valued at $3 million or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: From January 2018, the non-price weightage in the Price-Quality Tender Evaluation Method, which includes safety performance, will be raised from around 30% currently, to between 40% and 60%, for building construction projects valued at $3 million or more.

sections.label: Maximum fine for serious breaches
sections.summary: The $50,000 maximum fine applies to breaches that could reasonably cause death, serious bodily injury or dangerous occurrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: The $50,000 maximum fine will apply to breaches that could reasonably cause or result in death, serious bodily injury or dangerous occurrence.

sections.label: WSH courses migration to SSG
sections.summary: Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Alex Yam asked for an update on migration of WSH training providers' accreditation to SSG; 23 of 56 WSH courses have migrated to the WSQ Framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Alex Yam asked for an update on the migration of WSH training providers' accreditation to SSG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: So far, 23 of the 56 WSH courses have been successfully migrated to the WSQ Framework.

sections.label: Foreign construction worker retention rate
sections.summary: About 85% of all foreign construction workers had at least two years' experience as of June 2017, compared to 75% as of June 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Retention rate has also been improving, with about 85% of all foreign construction workers having at least two years' experience as of June 2017, compared to 75% as of June 2015.

sections.label: Employer safety equipment responsibilities
sections.summary: Employers must provide safety equipment and training and ensure workers understand machinery operating instructions; deducting these costs from salaries is illegal under the WSH Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Employers are responsible for providing safety equipment and training and for ensuring workers understand machinery operating instructions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: It is illegal under the WSH Act for employers to deduct safety equipment and training costs from their workers' salaries.

sections.label: Whistleblower protection under WSH Act
sections.summary: Dismissing or threatening to dismiss whistleblowers is an offence under the WSH Act, a point raised by Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Louis Ng.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Protection for whistleblowing is something both Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Louis Ng touched on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: It is an offence under the WSH Act to dismiss or threaten to dismiss whistleblowers.

sections.label: Technology improving workplace safety
sections.summary: MOM mandated data loggers in mobile cranes with up to $5,000 funding per crane, and launched a WSH Technology Challenge with up to $2 million in support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Technology, indeed, can be an enabler to improve WSH.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: We have, for example, mandated the installation of data loggers in mobile cranes, and this is supported by up to $5,000 funding per crane from MOM, which has improved mobile crane safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: We have recently launched the inaugural WSH Technology Challenge with up to $2 million in Government support to invite solutions from companies to improve work-related vehicular safety.
